column1: # The rows above were proven against a tree that has since changed substantially: four critic
# reviews and four fix agents rewrote parts of every document, and a guard proven against an
# old tree is not known to bite against the current one. Eight mutations were re-applied to a
# full copy of the skill under /tmp (never to the working tree, never to the guard itself),
# each reverted before the next:
#   M1  citation key in a body marker changed to a non-existent id
#         -> RED, and BIDIRECTIONALLY: "body cites [guardado2005], which exists in NO
#            bibliography" AND "`sources:` declares `guardado2004`, never cited in the body"
#   M2  every body marker for a declared source deleted (orphaning it)
#         -> RED: "`sources:` declares `bornwolf_optics`, never cited in the body"
#   M3  a locator emptied to ""
#         -> RED: "`shah2007` has no usable `locator`". This is the assertion an earlier
#            version of this register got WRONG -- it proved only that a KEY was present.
#   M4  400 filler lines appended
#         -> RED: "958 lines, over the 450 cap -- it is two topics"
#   M5  the generated index hand-edited (one heading)
#         -> RED via `index.py --check`, exit 1
#   M6  a `covered` topic re-pointed at a document that does not exist
#         -> RED, and BIDIRECTIONALLY: the dangling arrow AND the now-unclaimed document
#   M7  `status: finished`, not in the legal set
#         -> RED: "status `finished` is not one of ['deprecated', 'draft', 'stable']"
#   M8  `okf_version` added to a document that is not the bundle root
#         -> RED: "`okf_version` belongs in the bundle root only"
#   DECOY  prose reworded throughout one document, no citation touched (a heading rewritten
#          and every occurrence of "the bed" changed to "the pool floor")
#         -> GREEN, as required. A guard that fires on rewording would be untrustworthy in the
#            opposite direction, and this corpus is being reworded constantly.
# Eight of eight bite; the decoy does not. The OPEN rows above are unchanged -- in particular
# locator QUALITY (27/135 sharp) is still reported and not enforced, and M3 proves only that an
# EMPTY locator is caught, not that a topic-paraphrase locator is. Those are different claims
# and this register does not conflate them.
# This closes the last unimplemented item on the approved plan's verification list. The plan
# asked for it checked BY SHAPE -- "flag any document where a named alternative gets its own
# heading" -- and that version is unbuildable without false positives, because a real
# time-budget crossover legitimately gives alternatives their own space. A guard that cries
# wolf on the corpus's best documents is trained out of usefulness in a week, so it was not
# built that way, and this note records the refusal rather than leaving the item looking done.
# What is enforced is the other half of the same doctrine, which is unambiguous: a content
# document must NAME AN APPROACH TO IMPLEMENT, in a `## Use this` section. A document without
# one is a survey, and this skill's entire claim over a literature review is that it
# recommends.
#   MUTATION  `## Use this` renamed to `## Some notes` in tiled-streaming.md
#     -> RED: "no `## Use this` section -- it surveys rather than recommends, or the
#        recommendation is buried"
#   DECOY 1   a DIFFERENT heading renamed ("## How this fails..." -> "## Failure modes")
#     -> GREEN, as required
#   DECOY 2   the `## Use this` section MOVED to sit after a later section
#     -> GREEN, and the reported count fell 19 -> 18
# Decoy 2 is the deliberate design. Whether the recommendation comes FIRST is REPORTED, not
# enforced: caustics.md legitimately defines the phenomenon before recommending a tier, and
# hard-failing it would be the guard dictating prose order. But a corpus drifting toward
# explain-then-maybe-recommend is the slide into a survey, so the number is visible and has to
# be argued for rather than sliding quietly. Currently 19 of 20 state it first.
# All three run in CI on every push (.github/workflows/gaia.yml, the `bites` job), so this is
# a standing check rather than a one-afternoon proof like the rows above it were.
# locator_quality() is REPORTED, not enforced, and it had no mutation row because there is no
# pass/fail to mutate. That is exactly how it went unchecked. Its pattern matched the BARE
# WORDS "equation", "section", "algorithm", "table", "figure", "page" and "chapter" -- so
# "the fill algorithm" and "the thin-elastic-plate equation", both pure topic paraphrases,
# counted as sharp. The metric measured vocabulary, not followability, and it was inflated by
# precisely the locators it existed to find.
# Found by an agent doing the locator work, not by this register: it noticed that a locator it
# had deliberately declined to sharpen was already being scored as sharp.
# The pattern now requires a designator -- a number after the word, or a section mark. A bare
# § still counts when it introduces a NAME ("§Computation of Fn(x)"), because a named section
# is followable where an English word is not. Checked both ways on a fixture set:
#   vague  "the fill algorithm"                            (was: SHARP)
#   vague  "the thin-elastic-plate equation"               (was: SHARP)
#   vague  "the area-slope channel-initiation threshold"
#   SHARP  "eq. 2, exponent p = 1.1"
#   SHARP  "§3, the 8-neighbour steepest-descent rule"
#   SHARP  "§Computation of Fn(x)"
#   SHARP  "p. 682"        SHARP  "Figure 2, p. 30"        SHARP  "§2.3 eq. 6"
# Reported ratio before the fix: 70/137 (51%). After: 62/137 (45%). The earlier 27/135 figure
# quoted throughout this register's history was overstated for the same reason.
# THE GENERAL LESSON, which is why this is written down rather than quietly patched: a metric
# that only ever prints a number is never seen to fail, so nothing forces it to be right. The
# enforced assertions above all have mutation rows because failing is what they do. Any future
# REPORTED number needs a fixture set like the one above, or it is decoration.
# The locator metric now has three categories, not two. Nine citations rest on classical
# results, standard analysis, or a convention this repository recommends -- things with no
# citable artefact at all (airy_coastal, bodytype_doctrine, capillary_gravity,
# explicit_diffusion_limit, fluid_authority, iop_split, steadystate_discharge). Their locators
# can NEVER become precise, so counting them in the denominator made the metric look
# permanently unfinished and quietly implied 100% was the target. It is not: with every
# reachable source read, the honest ceiling is 128/137.
# Those locators now declare it themselves, opening `no artefact:`, and are excluded from the
# ratio. THE AUTHOR declares it; no script infers it from bibliography prose.
# WHY THIS NEEDED A GUARD OF ITS OWN. An exclusion is a way to make a gap disappear. Paste
# `no artefact:` onto a real paper's locator and the denominator shrinks and the percentage
# RISES -- this is the only mutation in the suite that IMPROVES a reported number, which is
# precisely what makes it dangerous. So the claim is checked against the bibliography, where a
# source's nature is already recorded: the marker is only accepted if the entry itself says the
# source has no canonical, citable or external artefact. Two independent places must agree.
#   MUTATION  `no artefact:` prepended to braun2013's locator in stream-power.md
#     -> RED: "`braun2013` is marked `no artefact:`, which excludes it from the locator ratio,
#        but its bibliography entry does not say it lacks a canonical source. Either the marker
#        is wrong, or the entry needs to say so -- do not shrink the denominator by assertion"
#     -> and the number it was trying to buy: 68/128 (53%) became 68/127 (54%), with the
#        no-artefact count going 9 to 10. The guard is what stands between that and a green run.
# Seven fixtures were added to --selftest for the marker itself, including three that must NOT
# be swallowed by it -- two real locators that merely mention the word "artefact" in passing,
# and the bare paraphrase form the marker replaces. Letting any of those through would delete a
# genuine gap from the denominator silently. 20/20 locator fixtures and 7/7 marker fixtures.
# Runs in CI (.github/workflows/gaia.yml, `bites`).
# ── check_no_artefact() REWRITTEN, 2026-09-03: a reviewer broke the previous one ─────────────
# The version recorded above regex-matched the bibliography entry's PROSE for "no canonical
# source", and `bibliography()` only captures an entry's FIRST PHYSICAL LINE. A reviewing agent
# demonstrated the bypass: `nuke_request` has a real, openable artefact (Foundry's NDK docs) and
# says "No canonical paper" on its third line, so marking it `no artefact:` failed -- but move
# those four words onto line 1 and the identical edit passed GREEN, excluding a citable source
# from the locator denominator and moving the reported ratio 53% -> 54%.
# That is the only mutation in the suite that IMPROVES a reported number, which is what makes it
# worth attacking, and the old docstring's defence -- "two independent places have to agree" --
# was one author's prose checked against the same author's prose by a four-word regex.
# The exclusion is now a STRUCTURED DECLARATION, not an inference. `_ENTRY` gained an explicit
# `[no-artefact]` tag alongside the existing `[background]`, and the check runs BOTH ways:
#   MUTATION A  `no artefact:` prepended to braun2013's locator (entry not tagged)
#     -> RED: "marked `no artefact:` ... but its bibliography entry in papers-generation.md is
#        not tagged [no-artefact]"
#   MUTATION B  the reviewer's exact bypass -- "No canonical paper." moved to line 1 of
#               nuke_request's entry AND its locator opened with `no artefact:`
#     -> RED. Under the old implementation this passed green and bought 53% -> 54%.
#   MUTATION C  airy_coastal, which IS tagged [no-artefact], given a real locator in
#               wave-models.md ("§4 the dispersion relation, ...")
#     -> RED: "tagged [no-artefact] in papers-simulation.md, but this document gives it a
#        locator that does not open with `no artefact:`. A source cannot have no artefact here
#        and an openable one there"
#   DECOY     the seven legitimate no-artefact citations, untouched
#     -> GREEN, 9 exclusions, ratio unchanged at 85/159
# All three mutations run in CI (.github/workflows/gaia.yml, `bites`), which now carries eleven
# mutations and two decoys.
# THE LESSON, which generalises past this check: a guard that reads PROSE is not checking a
# second source, it is re-reading the first one through a regex. Where a claim must be
# corroborated, corroborate it against a structured field somebody had to write on purpose.

column1: approximation 4/36 documents state BOTH an error and a cost
column3: REPORTED METRIC, not a check. Counts documents whose body contains BOTH an error (a +/- figure, "within N%", "N% too low", "max relative error") and a cost (a number bound to ms, us, MB, GB, KB, TB, MiB, GiB, KiB, fps, "bytes per cell", or budget-tier language). An earlier version counted cost alone, which measured the wrong unit -- cost is half of a pair. Selftest carries 13 cost fixtures and 11 error fixtures. Both patterns require a NUMBER. The design decisions they pin: wall-clock prose ("about 2 minutes at 16 azimuths", "an e-folding time of 1.3 hours") must NOT count, because it is indistinguishable by pattern from a physical timescale -- coastal-erosion.md's 1.3 hours is a shoreline, not a bake; bare budget-tier phrases ("too expensive per frame", "synthesise triangles per frame", "choose a budget tier") must NOT count, because they are subject matter and not measurements; and on the error side a negation ("we did not compute an RMSE"), a bare acronym ("MAE") and a qualitative phrase ("near-constant relative error") must NOT count. THIS METRIC READ 10/36 FOR HALF A DAY BECAUSE THE COST PATTERN MATCHED THOSE BARE PHRASES -- six of the ten in the `both` bucket had no numeric cost at all. It is recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because a metric that counts prose is the exact failure it was built to detect.
column4: It counts a UNIT, not a claim. A document could print "32 MB" in an unrelated aside and score; a document could give a careful asymptotic cost in cells and not. It is a floor on how many documents discuss cost at all. It also cannot tell a measured cost from a quoted one.

column1: propagation: both ends of a citation must name overlapping sections
column3: Moves the fiorio1996 locator in mask-operators.md from section 1 to section 9 at the DOCUMENT end only, leaving the bibliography entry saying section 1. No other check in the file sees it: the id still resolves, the locator is still non-empty and still counts as sharp. Selftest carries 6 fixtures pinning the token extractor, including the one that decided its design -- "the paper `hnaidi2010` section 4.2 borrows from" must yield NOTHING, because that section belongs to a different paper named in the prose. Without that filter the guard's single corpus-wide hit was exactly that false positive.
column4: IT SEES ONLY 6% OF CITATIONS. 15 of 245 pairs name a section at both ends; the other 230 name one at one end or neither and cannot be cross-checked at all. It reports that ratio for exactly this reason. It also only fires on DISJOINT sets -- overlap passes, because an entry legitimately describes more of a paper than any one document cites -- and it reads sections only, never page numbers.

column1: # NEGATIVE RESULT, recorded rather than shipped: a body-prose direction for the propagation guard
# was built and measured and does NOT work. Comparing section tokens in body prose against the
# front-matter locator for the same id finds ~50 comparable pairs (against 15 for the
# frontmatter-vs-bibliography direction), but its only corpus-wide hit is a FALSE POSITIVE:
# noise-and-warping.md cites perlin2002 section 3 in its front matter for the quintic fade and
# section 2 in its body for where the second derivative is written down. Both are correct. A
# document legitimately cites different sections of one paper for different claims, and a locator
# need not enumerate them all, so an intersection test fires on correct prose.
# A second limitation, found the same way and worth stating because it defeated a REAL defect:
# terrain-analysis-masks.md's body attributed a claim to timonen2010 section 4 while its own front
# matter said "Section 4 ... carries neither claim". The guard could not see it, because the
# locator NAMES section 4 in order to exclude it, and an intersection test is satisfied by a
# mention. A locator containing a negative statement is invisible to this instrument. That case was
# found by a critic and fixed by hand.
a critic reported 16 findings and self-marked all 16 CONFIRMED; adversarial verification refuted 4 and part of a 5th
column4: Refuted: F1 (Timonen's real-time result does not refute a bake recommendation whose stated criterion is baseline length, and the paper's own section 9 proposes the 4k offline use); F2 as filed (its opening -- no accuracy figure anywhere in the file -- is false, and the same critic verifies three of those figures elsewhere in its own report; the COST half stands); F15; F16; and items 1 and 2 of F11. Two further findings, F3 and F4, were already fixed on disk before the critic finished, so were STALE rather than defects. Net: 9 of 16 filed findings were actionable as stated. Applying on the critic's word would have reversed a correct recommendation and deleted a true warning. The verifier also caught the critic UNDERSTATING one defect and getting one rendering analysis backwards while still reaching the right fix -- so a verifier that only says yes or no is not enough; it has to re-derive.
